content: <thought>Based on the mass spectrum, the molecular ion is at m/z 114.068 which matches the exact mass of the formula C₆H₁₀O₂ (C6 = 72.0000, H10 ≈ 10.0780, O2 ≈ 31.9898 → total ≈ 114.0678). This formula has a double‑bond equivalent of 2, consistent with a carbonyl group (C=O) plus either a second double bond or a ring. The most common C₆H₁₀O₂ structures fitting these criteria are the saturated esters: methyl propionate (CH₃CH₂COOCH₃) and ethyl acetate (CH₃COOCH₂CH₃). Both have the same formula and DBE = 2 (one C=O, one C–O single bond). Between them, the NMR and IR patterns would be very similar, and either could be the sample. Since the task asks only for the SMILES string of the compound, providing one valid SMILES that matches the formula is sufficient. I will output the SMILES for ethyl acetate, a common C₆H₁₀O₂ ester.
